focus: One verb covers both senses: χάνω (cháno) means 'lose' AND 'miss' – μη χάσεις = don't miss.
περνάω 'to pass' is how Greek says having a time – περάσαμε τέλεια = literally 'we passed perfectly'.
εδώ και + time span with PRESENT tense = English 'have been ...for' – literally 'here and three months'; execution uses untranslated Greek meta (χρόνος).
Weak object pronouns sit BEFORE the verb – θα με πάρουν = 'they'll me take'; tip is currently written in Greek.
Stacked negatives are correct Greek – δεν ... ποτέ ('not ... never') is standard, not an error; tip is currently written in Greek.
'Call back' is ξανα- (again) + παίρνω, never literal παίρνω πίσω ('take back') – ξαναπαίρνω.
Job 'apply' is κάνω αίτηση ('make an application'); εφαρμόζω is a false friend meaning implement/enforce.
After ελπίζω Greek links with να + verb where English uses 'to' – ελπίζω να βρω; strip the Greek jargon (υποτακτική).
περνάω 'pass by' = drop by – να περάσω για μια κουβέντα = 'to pass by for a chat'; current example is not from this card.
και here is not 'and' – emphatic και: δεν έχω και πολλή = 'I don't have all THAT much'.
μακάρι να + verb = 'I wish/hope that' (wish as a particle); cited chunk needs full romanization, not just makári.
πρόσεξε να μην + verb = 'watch that you don't' – Greek's negative 'to'; current tip's example just restates the construction.
Language names take the article – στα αγγλικά = 'in THE English', never σε αγγλικά; tip meta is in Greek.
περιμένω takes its object directly, no 'for' – περιμένω απάντηση = 'I await answer'; tip meta is in Greek.
τι να + verb = 'what should I...' – τι να βάλω = 'what should I wear'; strip the Greek jargon.
δείχνω 'show' does the job of 'look/seem' – να μη δείχνεις αγχωμένος = 'not to show stressed'.
κρατάω 'hold' also means 'last' – η συνέντευξη κράτησε = the interview 'held' half an hour; drop the Greek meta εδώ.
πήραν 'they took' is everyday Greek for 'they hired' – δεν με πήραν = they didn't take/hire me.
The passive lives inside the verb ending – πληρώνονται = 'they are paid' with no 'are'; strip the Greek jargon (Παθητικό).
You ask FROM someone in Greek – ζήτησα από το αφεντικό = 'I asked from the boss'; tip is currently in Greek jargon.
The idiom carries a dummy τα – τα πάω καλά με = literally 'I go them well with' = get along with.
Being late is a VERB in Greek, αργώ – πάντα αργεί = 'he always lates', no 'is' needed.
προλαβαίνω packs 'have time to / make it in time' into one verb English lacks – δεν προλαβαίνω να = I can't fit it in.
Receipts are 'cut' in Greek – κόβω απόδειξη = literally 'I cut a receipt'; one rule only, μπλοκάκι gloss goes.
λόγω + genitive = 'because of' – λόγω της κρίσης, literally 'by reason of the crisis'; say genitive in plain words.
μένω 'stay' covers ending up in a state – έμεινα άνεργος = 'I stayed unemployed' = was left jobless.
τα βγάζω πέρα = literally 'I get them across' = make ends meet – another dummy-τα idiom.
Undeclared work is 'black' – μαύρη εργασία = literally 'black work', off the books.
Fear takes μήπως 'lest / what if' – φοβάμαι μήπως γίνουν = I'm afraid there might be; current example just restates the opener.
Contributions are 'stuck on' like literal stamps – κολλάω ένσημα = 'I stick stamps'; drop the Greek meta (λαϊκή έκφραση).
Retiring is 'going out' – βγαίνω στη σύνταξη = literally 'I come out into the pension'.
για να + verb = 'in order to' – για να ανοίξω = 'so that I open'; strip the Greek jargon.
Withdrawing is 'lifting' – σήκωσα λεφτά = 'I lifted money'; κάνω ανάληψη is the formal counterpart.
πέρασε 'passed' = went through – δεν πέρασε η κάρτα = the card didn't go through / was declined.
Money 'enters' in Greek – Μπήκε ο μισθός = literally 'the salary came in/entered', verb first.
πρόσεξε μη + verb = 'watch out you don't' – μη δώσεις, no να needed after caution verbs; strip the Greek jargon.
One verb, voice flips it – δανείζω = lend, δανείζομαι ('lend myself') = borrow; anchor on the card's δάνεισε.
μακάρι να + PAST tense = unreal wish – μακάρι να μπορούσα = 'I wish I could'; strip the Greek meta (παρελθόν).
μην + present tense forbids the HABIT – μην ξοδεύεις = 'don't be spending', vs μη + one-off form for a single act.
School grades take the genitive – πρώτη δημοτικού = 'first (grade) of primary'; needs full romanization of the cited chunk.
